lessons.title: Every Fortune Starts as a Burning Desire
lessons.key_idea: Hill argues achievement begins with an intense, specific desire, illustrated by Edwin Barnes, who resolved to become Thomas Edison's business partner and eventually did.

lessons.title: Six Steps to Turn Wishes into Goals
lessons.key_idea: Hill's method turns a vague wish into a definite goal: name an exact amount, decide what you will give, set a date, make a plan, write it down, and read it aloud twice daily.

lessons.title: Faith and Autosuggestion Reprogram Your Mind
lessons.key_idea: Hill claims that repeating your written goal with emotion plants it in your subconscious and builds the belief that drives action.

lessons.title: Knowledge Only Matters When Put to Work
lessons.key_idea: Hill insists knowledge is only potential power until imagination organizes it into a practical plan, so you can borrow expertise you lack rather than know everything yourself.

lessons.title: Build a Master Mind Team
lessons.key_idea: Hill says an organized plan backed by a small group of people working in harmony toward one goal achieves far more than any individual alone.

lessons.title: Decide Fast, Persist Longer
lessons.key_idea: Hill warns against quitting too soon, using the story of R. U. Darby, who abandoned a gold mine just three feet short of a rich vein that the next owner found.

lessons.title: Defeat the Ghosts of Fear
lessons.key_idea: Hill ties his principles together by naming six basic fears, including fear of poverty and criticism, and arguing that desire, faith, planning, and persistence together are how you overcome them.

plan.title: Think and Grow Rich
plan.author: Napoleon Hill
plan.confidence_note: I know this widely read 1937 classic in detail, including its thirteen principles, its six-step method for desire, and its best-known stories, though Hill's claims about his research are historically disputed.
plan.one_liner: A century-old playbook claiming success starts with one burning desire and a mind trained to chase it.
plan.summary: Napoleon Hill says he spent years studying hundreds of successful people, prompted by the industrialist Andrew Carnegie, to find a shared formula for achievement. The result is thirteen principles, starting with the idea that every fortune begins as a thought. Hill argues you need a burning desire for a specific goal, written down with a deadline and a plan, and repeated daily until your subconscious believes it. He stresses that knowledge only matters when organized into action, that imagination turns ideas into plans, and that a small group of allies, which he calls a Master Mind, multiplies your power. Quick decisions and stubborn persistence carry you past setbacks, and Hill warns that fears such as poverty and criticism quietly sabotage most people. His core claim is that mindset, applied with discipline, shapes results.
